categories.name: Cloud & Infrastructure
categories.description: Cloud-native infrastructure, deployment, and scaling across modern providers. We architect resilient, auto-scaling systems on Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and hybrid environments — from compute and storage to managed ML services and global networking.

categories.name: DevOps & CI/CD
categories.description: Automation, containerization, and continuous delivery pipelines. We build end-to-end DevOps workflows with Git-based version control, container orchestration, automated testing gates, and reproducible deployments across staging and production.

categories.name: Backend & Enterprise
categories.description: Enterprise-grade backend services and frameworks powering mission-critical workloads. Our teams build secure, scalable APIs and microservices with Spring Boot, Express, and battle-tested Java/Python stacks backed by strong data persistence layers.

categories.name: Databases
categories.description: Relational and NoSQL data stores for modern applications. We design schemas, tune queries, and operate high-availability clusters across MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MongoDB, and in-memory stores to meet performance, durability, and compliance requirements.

categories.name: Mobile Development
categories.description: Cross-platform and native mobile application development for iOS and Android. We ship polished, high-performance apps using Flutter and Dart for cross-platform reach, and Kotlin/Java with Jetpack Compose for deeply native experiences.

categories.name: Frontend & Web
categories.description: Modern web interfaces, frameworks, and web standards. We build fast, accessible, SEO-friendly applications with React, Next.js, and TypeScript — backed by strong engineering around performance budgets, Core Web Vitals, and design-system consistency.

categories.name: AI & Machine Learning
categories.description: Artificial intelligence, ML models, and intelligent systems. From data preprocessing and model training to LLM-powered applications, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, computer vision, OCR, and NLP — we deliver production-grade AI features grounded in evaluation and monitoring.

categories.name: Real-Time & Networking
categories.description: Low-latency communication, streaming, and networking protocols. We build live audio/video, chat, presence, and multiplayer-style experiences with WebRTC, WebSocket, P2P, TURN/STUN traversal, and streaming stacks — engineered for reliability across NATs, firewalls, and mobile networks.

categories.name: Security
categories.description: Authentication, encryption, and secure infrastructure. We design defense-in-depth systems with modern token-based auth (JWT), TLS/SSL enforcement, firewalling, and least-privilege access — aligned with OWASP and enterprise compliance baselines.

categories.name: Operating Systems
categories.description: Operating systems and runtime environments. Our infrastructure runs on hardened Linux distributions like Ubuntu, tuned for containers, orchestration, and predictable performance at scale.

technologies.name: Oracle
technologies.description: Oracle provides enterprise-grade relational databases and a full cloud platform (OCI) for mission-critical workloads. We use Oracle Database for transactional integrity and advanced analytics, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for compute, storage, and enterprise-grade networking — enabling high-availability deployments, disaster recovery, and regulatory-compliant operations.
highlights: Oracle Database and Exadata for high-throughput OLTP
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) compute, storage, and networking
Real Application Clusters (RAC) for high availability and zero-downtime failover
Advanced security, audit vault, and data encryption at rest and in transit
PL/SQL stored procedures and database-native business logic

technologies.name: Google Cloud
technologies.description: Google Cloud is a comprehensive cloud platform offering scalable compute, managed data services, and enterprise ML tooling. We use GCP to build global, auto-scaling backends, run containerized workloads on GKE, store structured and unstructured data in BigQuery and Cloud Storage, and deliver AI features via Vertex AI — all with strong IAM, VPC networking, and cost-optimization discipline.
highlights: Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run for elastic workloads
BigQuery and Cloud Storage for analytics and durable object storage
Vertex AI for managed ML training, deployment, and model monitoring
IAM, VPC Service Controls, and Cloud Armor for secure networking
Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy for CI/CD and reproducible releases

technologies.name: GCP
technologies.description: GCP (Google Cloud Platform) provides the building blocks for modern cloud-native applications. We use GCP's managed services to ship faster — serverless functions, managed databases, message queues, and observability — while relying on Google's global network for low-latency delivery to users anywhere in the world.
highlights: Cloud Run and App Engine for serverless deployments
Cloud SQL, Firestore, and Spanner for managed data
Cloud Logging, Monitoring, and Trace for full observability

technologies.name: CI/CD
technologies.description: CI/CD is the practice of automating the build, test, and deployment of software to deliver changes quickly and safely. We design pipelines that run unit, integration, and end-to-end tests on every commit, enforce code-quality and security gates, and deploy to staging and production with rolling, blue-green, or canary strategies — reducing lead time and release risk.
highlights: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins pipelines
Automated unit, integration, and end-to-end testing gates
Static analysis, security scanning, and dependency checks

technologies.name: Git & GitHub
technologies.description: Git is the distributed version control system that underpins all modern software collaboration, and GitHub is its most widely adopted platform. We use Git branching strategies like GitFlow and trunk-based development to keep changes reviewable, enforce code ownership and review policies via pull requests, and integrate CI/CD directly into the development workflow.
highlights: Pull requests, code reviews, and CODEOWNERS enforcement
GitHub Actions for CI/CD and automation
Branch protection rules and signed commits

technologies.name: Docker
technologies.description: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into portable containers that run identically across developer laptops, CI runners, and production clusters. We use multi-stage builds to keep images small, Compose for local multi-service development, and container registries for secure, versioned image distribution — the foundation for reproducible deployment.
highlights: Multi-stage Dockerfiles for small, secure images
Docker Compose for local multi-service development
Private registries with image signing and scanning
Integration with Kubernetes and cloud container runtimes

technologies.name: Containers
technologies.description: Container orchestration (primarily Kubernetes) schedules, scales, heals, and networks containers across clusters. We run production workloads on Kubernetes and managed services like GKE, leveraging Helm charts, autoscaling, rolling updates, and service mesh networking to deliver resilient, observable systems.
highlights: Kubernetes clusters on GKE, EKS, or self-managed
Helm charts for templated, versioned deployments
Rolling updates, health probes, and self-healing
Service mesh (Istio/Linkerd) for secure service-to-service traffic

technologies.name: Firebase
technologies.description: Firebase is Google's backend-as-a-service platform providing realtime databases, authentication, hosting, and serverless functions. We use Firebase to ship features quickly — realtime sync with Firestore, secure auth with Firebase Auth, static and dynamic hosting, and Cloud Functions for event-driven logic — while keeping costs predictable and scaling with demand.
highlights: Firestore and Realtime Database for realtime sync
Firebase Authentication with social and enterprise identity
Cloud Functions for serverless backend logic
Firebase Hosting with global CDN and SSL
Firebase Cloud Messaging for cross-platform push notifications

technologies.name: Redis
technologies.description: Redis is a high-performance in-memory data store used for caching, session storage, real-time leaderboards, and pub/sub messaging. We use Redis to reduce database load, accelerate hot reads, and enable low-latency features like rate limiting and distributed locks — often paired with a durable primary database for persistence.
highlights: Caching and session storage with sub-millisecond latency
Pub/Sub messaging and streams for event fan-out
Sorted sets for leaderboards and rate limiting
High availability via Redis Sentinel and Cluster

technologies.name: Kafka
technologies.description: Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform for high-throughput, fault-tolerant data pipelines. We use Kafka to decouple services, power event-driven architectures, and stream data between producers and consumers with strong durability and ordering guarantees — enabling real-time analytics, change data capture, and reactive microservices.
highlights: High-throughput topics with partitioning and replication
Kafka Streams and ksqlDB for stream processing
Connect for CDC and external system integration

technologies.name: NGINX
technologies.description: NGINX is a high-performance web server, reverse proxy, and load balancer. We use NGINX to terminate TLS, route traffic to backend services, serve static assets with aggressive caching, and balance load across instances — providing a reliable front door for our applications and APIs.
highlights: Reverse proxy and load balancing across backends
TLS/SSL termination with modern cipher suites
Static asset serving with gzip/brotli and caching
Rate limiting, connection limits, and access control

technologies.name: Firewall
technologies.description: Firewalls are the first line of network defense, controlling traffic between trusted and untrusted networks. We use cloud-native and host-based firewalls to enforce least-privilege access, isolate environments, and block malicious traffic — combined with WAF and DDoS protection for defense-in-depth.
highlights: Packet filtering and stateful rule sets

technologies.name: Jenkins
technologies.description: Jenkins is an extensible automation server for building, testing, and deploying software. We use Jenkins pipelines-as-code to define reproducible CI/CD workflows, integrate with source control and container registries, and orchestrate complex multi-stage releases across environments.
highlights: Distributed builds with agents and controllers
Parallel and matrix builds for fast feedback
Integration with Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud providers

technologies.name: Deep Learning
technologies.description: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks to learn hierarchical representations from data. We apply CNNs for vision, RNNs and Transformers for sequence and language tasks, and transfer learning to bootstrap high-performing models from pretrained foundations — with careful evaluation, regularization, and deployment discipline.
highlights: CNNs for image classification and detection
RNNs and Transformers for sequence modeling
Transfer learning from pretrained foundation models
Model quantization and deployment to edge and cloud

technologies.name: Machine Learning
technologies.description: Machine learning is the practice of building systems that improve from data. We cover the full ML lifecycle — data preparation, feature engineering, model selection, training, evaluation, and deployment — with a focus on reproducibility, monitoring, and alignment with real business metrics.
highlights: Feature engineering and data pipeline design
Model evaluation, cross-validation, and bias checks

technologies.name: TensorFlow
technologies.description: TensorFlow is Google's open-source framework for building and training machine learning models at scale. We use its Keras high-level API for fast iteration, TensorBoard for experiment visualization, TF Serving for production inference, and TF Lite for mobile and edge deployment.
highlights: Keras high-level API for rapid prototyping
TF Serving for scalable production inference
TF Lite for mobile and edge deployment
Distributed training across GPUs and TPUs

technologies.name: Matplotlib
technologies.description: Matplotlib is Python's foundational plotting library for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations. We use it for exploratory data analysis, model evaluation reports, and scientific-quality figures — with fine-grained control over layout, styling, and annotation.
highlights: Line, bar, scatter, and histogram plots
Seamless integration with NumPy and Pandas

technologies.name: TF Lite
technologies.description: TensorFlow Lite is a lightweight ML runtime for deploying models on mobile, embedded, and edge devices. We use TF Lite to run inference locally on Android and iOS, enabling low-latency, privacy-preserving, and offline-capable AI features.
highlights: On-device inference for Android and iOS
Model quantization for smaller, faster models
Integration with Flutter and native SDKs

technologies.name: RAG
technologies.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines vector search with large language models to ground AI responses in authoritative, up-to-date knowledge. We build RAG pipelines with embedding models, vector databases, and prompt construction strategies that reduce hallucinations and keep answers accurate and citable.
highlights: Prompt grounding and citation of sources
Evaluation of retrieval precision and answer quality

technologies.name: Agentic AI
technologies.description: Agentic AI systems plan, reason, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously with tools and memory. We build tool-calling agents, multi-agent orchestration pipelines, and reflection loops to automate complex workflows — with guardrails, observability, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints for safety.

technologies.name: Generative AI
technologies.description: Generative AI creates new text, images, code, and audio using LLMs and diffusion models. We integrate generative capabilities into products via APIs, fine-tuning, and LoRA adapters — while enforcing safety, moderation, and cost controls.
highlights: LLM text generation and chat experiences
Cost, latency, and token budget controls

technologies.name: LLM
technologies.description: Large Language Models are transformer-based neural networks capable of reasoning, generation, and conversation. We use LLMs for chat, summarization, extraction, and code assistance, and apply prompt engineering, structured outputs, and instruction tuning to make them reliable for production use.

technologies.name: Neural Network
technologies.description: Neural networks are layered systems of neurons that learn representations directly from data. We design and train networks for classification, regression, and generation — with careful attention to architecture, initialization, regularization, and optimization.
highlights: Architecture design for vision, text, and tabular data
Debugging with loss curves and gradient checks

technologies.name: Data Preprocessing
technologies.description: Data preprocessing transforms raw data into a clean, consistent form suitable for ML. We handle missing values, outliers, and inconsistencies; normalize and scale features; encode categorical variables; and construct reproducible pipelines that prevent train/test leakage.

technologies.name: Model Training
technologies.description: Model training is the iterative process of fitting a model to data, validating performance, and tuning hyperparameters. We train with proper splits, cross-validation, and experiment tracking, and we balance compute cost against accuracy and generalization.
highlights: Experiment tracking with MLflow or W&B
Distributed training across GPUs and TPUs
Reproducibility via seeds and versioned data

technologies.name: Computer Vision
technologies.description: Computer vision enables machines to interpret images and video. We build classification, object detection, segmentation, and pose estimation pipelines using modern CNNs and Vision Transformers, and we optimize them for real-time inference on edge and cloud.
highlights: Image classification with CNNs and ViTs

technologies.name: OCR
technologies.description: Optical Character Recognition extracts text from images and PDFs, enabling document automation. We use modern OCR engines like Tesseract and EasyOCR combined with layout parsing to reliably extract structured data from invoices, IDs, and forms.

technologies.name: NLP
technologies.description: Natural Language Processing enables machines to understand and generate human language. We build text classification, sentiment analysis, named entity recognition, and semantic search pipelines using modern embeddings and transformer models.
highlights: Named entity recognition and relation extraction

technologies.name: Spring Boot
technologies.description: Spring Boot is the standard for production-ready Java backend services. It provides auto-configuration, embedded servers, and a rich ecosystem for building REST APIs, GraphQL endpoints, and microservices — with first-class support for security, data access, and observability.
highlights: Spring Security for auth and authorization
Actuator metrics, health checks, and observability

technologies.name: Flask
technologies.description: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework for building APIs and microservices. We use Flask for ML model serving, internal tools, and small-to-medium REST services — with extensions for ORM, validation, and auth when needed.
highlights: ML model serving and inference endpoints

technologies.name: Hibernate
technologies.description: Hibernate is a mature ORM for Java that maps objects to relational tables. We use Hibernate to persist domain entities, manage relationships and transactions, and tune lazy loading and caching for performance.

technologies.name: Spring Core
technologies.description: Spring Core provides the inversion-of-control (IoC) container and dependency injection foundation for all Spring applications. We use Spring Core to wire beans, manage lifecycles, and apply aspect-oriented programming for cross-cutting concerns.

technologies.name: JPA
technologies.description: The Java Persistence API (JPA) standardizes object-relational mapping in Java. We use JPA (usually with Hibernate) to define entities, manage transactions, and query databases with JPQL in a portable, vendor-neutral way.

technologies.name: JDBC
technologies.description: JDBC is the low-level Java API for executing SQL against relational databases. We use JDBC for fine-grained control over queries, batching, and connection pooling — and for scenarios where an ORM adds unnecessary overhead.
highlights: Prepared statements and SQL injection prevention

technologies.name: Servlet
technologies.description: Java Servlets are server-side components that handle HTTP requests and responses. We use servlets (often via Spring MVC) to build web endpoints with session management, filters, and listeners — the foundation of the Java web stack.
highlights: Integration with Spring MVC and Boot

technologies.name: ORM
technologies.description: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) bridges objects in application code and relational tables in the database. We apply ORM patterns to keep domain logic clean, map relationships explicitly, and avoid common pitfalls like N+1 queries and uncontrolled eager loading.

technologies.name: ExpressJS
technologies.description: Express is a fast, minimalist web framework for Node.js. We use Express to build REST APIs, middleware pipelines, and small-to-medium backend services where a lightweight, unopinionated foundation is ideal.

technologies.name: MySQL
technologies.description: MySQL is one of the most widely used open-source relational databases. We use MySQL for OLTP workloads, reporting, and web applications — with strong ACID guarantees, replication, and clustering for availability.

technologies.name: MongoDB
technologies.description: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with flexible schemas. We use MongoDB for content management, product catalogs, real-time analytics, and applications where evolving data shapes are common — with strong aggregation and horizontal scaling.

technologies.name: PostgreSQL
technologies.description: PostgreSQL is an advanced open-source relational database known for standards compliance and extensibility. We use PostgreSQL for OLTP, geospatial data (PostGIS), JSON workloads (JSONB), and full-text search — often as the default choice for new projects.

technologies.name: Hive
technologies.description: Apache Hive provides a SQL-like interface for querying large datasets stored in Hadoop. We use Hive for batch analytics, ETL, and data warehousing on distributed storage — pairing it with modern engines like Spark for performance.
highlights: Integration with Hadoop HDFS and Spark

technologies.name: OracleDB
technologies.description: Oracle Database is an enterprise-grade relational database designed for high availability, security, and performance. We use OracleDB for mission-critical workloads requiring strict transaction guarantees, advanced security, and proven scalability.

technologies.name: MariaDB
technologies.description: MariaDB is a community-developed fork of MySQL with performance improvements and additional storage engines. We use MariaDB as a drop-in MySQL replacement for web applications, with strong compatibility and open governance.

technologies.name: InnoDB
technologies.description: InnoDB is the default ACID-compliant storage engine for MySQL and MariaDB. It provides row-level locking, foreign keys, and crash recovery — the foundation for reliable transactional workloads.

technologies.name: Flutter
technologies.description: Flutter is Google's UI toolkit for building beautiful, high-performance mobile apps from a single Dart codebase. We use Flutter for iOS and Android (and web/desktop) to ship fast, consistent interfaces with expressive custom widgets and native platform integration.
highlights: Single Dart codebase for iOS, Android, web, and desktop
Expressive custom widget and animation system
Native platform channels for device features

technologies.name: Dart
technologies.description: Dart is the modern, strongly typed language powering Flutter. It supports null safety, async/await, streams, and ahead-of-time compilation to native code — enabling predictable performance across platforms.

technologies.name: Kotlin
technologies.description: Kotlin is the modern, concise language for native Android development. We use Kotlin with coroutines and Jetpack Compose to build responsive, maintainable apps with full access to the Android SDK and ecosystem.
highlights: Coroutines and Flow for async programming

technologies.name: Java Android
technologies.description: Java is the classic language for Android development, with a mature ecosystem, robust tooling, and broad library support. We maintain and extend Java-based Android apps alongside Kotlin for legacy and hybrid projects.
highlights: Interop with Kotlin in the same project

technologies.name: Cross Platform
technologies.description: Cross-platform development maximizes code reuse across iOS, Android, web, and desktop while preserving native-quality UX. We use Flutter and shared architecture to reduce cost and speed time-to-market without sacrificing performance.

technologies.name: Native C++
technologies.description: C++ delivers low-level performance and control critical for graphics, game engines, and performance-sensitive mobile modules. We use the Android NDK and JNI to integrate C++ into mobile apps for CPU-bound workloads and cross-platform shared libraries.

technologies.name: Android Studio
technologies.description: Android Studio is the official IDE for Android development, offering emulators, layout inspectors, profilers, and Gradle build tooling. Our Android team uses Android Studio for fast iteration, debugging, and performance profiling.
highlights: Profiler for CPU, memory, and network

technologies.name: ReactJS
technologies.description: React is the leading library for building interactive user interfaces with components. We use React with hooks, context, and modern state management to build scalable, maintainable frontends with strong ecosystem support.
highlights: Hooks and context for state management

technologies.name: Next.js
technologies.description: Next.js is the production framework for React, with server-side rendering, static generation, API routes, and edge support. We use Next.js for high-performance, SEO-friendly, full-stack web apps — combining server components with client interactivity.
highlights: SSR, SSG, and ISR rendering modes

technologies.name: TypeScript
technologies.description: TypeScript adds static typing to JavaScript, catching bugs at compile time and improving developer experience across large codebases. We use TypeScript across frontend and backend for safer refactors and richer IDE tooling.
highlights: Strong integration with React and Node.js

technologies.name: JavaScript
technologies.description: JavaScript is the language of the web, powering interactive frontends and Node.js backends. We write modern ES2023+ JavaScript with async/await, modules, and functional patterns, and TypeScript where stronger guarantees are needed.

technologies.name: TSX
technologies.description: TSX is the TypeScript extension for writing typed React components. We use TSX for type-safe props, state, and events — reducing runtime errors and improving team velocity in large React codebases.

technologies.name: XML
technologies.description: XML is a markup language for structured data, configuration, and Android layouts. We use XML for Android view layouts, configuration files, and standardized data interchange.

technologies.name: JSON
technologies.description: JSON is the ubiquitous lightweight data-interchange format used across APIs, configs, and NoSQL databases. We work with JSON extensively for API payloads, configuration, and structured data — with schema validation where correctness matters.

technologies.name: SEO
technologies.description: SEO (Search Engine Optimization) improves discoverability and ranking on search engines. We optimize technical SEO (crawlability, metadata, Core Web Vitals, structured data) alongside content strategy to drive organic traffic.
highlights: Meta tags, sitemaps, and robots directives
Core Web Vitals and performance budgets

technologies.name: WebRTC
technologies.description: WebRTC enables low-latency, peer-to-peer audio, video, and data streaming directly in the browser. We use WebRTC for video calls, live collaboration, and real-time data channels — with STUN/TURN infrastructure for reliable connectivity.

technologies.name: WebSocket
technologies.description: WebSocket provides persistent, full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection. We use WebSocket for live chat, notifications, presence, and real-time dashboards — with reconnection, backpressure, and message ordering handled explicitly.

technologies.name: P2P
technologies.description: Peer-to-peer (P2P) networking connects clients directly, reducing server load and latency. We use P2P via WebRTC data channels for file transfer, collaborative editing, and media streaming — with NAT traversal and fallbacks for restrictive networks.

technologies.name: Streaming
technologies.description: Streaming delivers live and on-demand audio/video with low latency and adaptive quality. We implement HLS and DASH streaming with adaptive bitrate, CDN distribution, and LL-HLS for interactive live use cases.

technologies.name: FCM
technologies.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) delivers reliable push notifications across Android, iOS, and web. We use FCM for user engagement, transactional alerts, and topic-based broadcasts — with delivery tracking and fallback channels.
highlights: Push notifications for Android, iOS, and web

technologies.name: TURN Server
technologies.description: A TURN (Traversal Using Relays around NAT) server relays media when direct peer-to-peer connections fail. We deploy TURN servers with coturn and cloud relaying to guarantee WebRTC connectivity across restrictive firewalls and symmetric NATs.
highlights: Relays media streams when P2P fails
Traverses strict firewalls and symmetric NATs

technologies.name: STUN Server
technologies.description: A STUN (Session Traversal Utilities for NAT) server helps peers discover their public IP and port, enabling direct P2P connections. We use STUN as the first step in WebRTC ICE to establish low-latency connections.
highlights: NAT discovery and public IP resolution

technologies.name: UDP
technologies.description: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless transport with low latency and no built-in reliability. We use UDP for real-time media (WebRTC, QUIC) and streaming where timeliness matters more than guaranteed delivery.

technologies.name: REST API
technologies.description: REST is a stateless, resource-oriented API architecture built on HTTP. We design REST APIs with consistent conventions, proper status codes, pagination, and versioning — documented with OpenAPI for robust client generation and testing.

technologies.name: JWT
technologies.description: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) provide stateless authentication and authorization via signed tokens. We use JWTs for API access, single sign-on, and role-based authorization — with short expiry, refresh tokens, and revocation strategies.

technologies.name: SSL
technologies.description: SSL/TLS encrypts data in transit, protecting user credentials, tokens, and sensitive payloads. We enforce HTTPS everywhere, automate certificate management, and configure modern cipher suites to comply with security best practices.

technologies.name: Linux
technologies.description: Linux is the open-source operating system powering most of the cloud. We run production infrastructure, containers, and CI runners on Linux — with hardening, observability, and automation via systemd, shell scripting, and configuration management.
highlights: Server and container host operating system

technologies.name: Ubuntu
technologies.description: Ubuntu is the most widely used Debian-based Linux distribution for servers, cloud images, and developer workstations. We use Ubuntu LTS releases for stable, long-supported production systems with strong ecosystem and cloud image support.
highlights: Cloud images and container base images
